title: Keeping natural gas flowing after historic Colorado floods
summary: Restoring critical infrastructure while keeping natural gas flowing to thousands of customers
body_markdown:
In October 2026, severe flooding in southwest Colorado washed out homes, roads and bridges. Along the Piedra River, floodwaters damaged a natural gas pipeline near Chimney Rock. The damage threatened natural gas service to communities across southwest Colorado, just as colder temperatures were approaching.


Crews responded immediately, isolating the damaged section of pipeline and beginning a complex, weeks-long effort to maintain service and develop a temporary repair.


The challenges were significant. With roads closed, response teams had limited access to the pipeline to assess the damage and make repairs. A second round of historic flooding further complicated the effort, forcing crews to temporarily suspend repair work while prioritizing employee safety.


Behind the scenes, teams from across Xcel Energy worked around the clock to keep natural gas flowing. Engineers developed solutions to reinforce the system while field crews established temporary compressed natural gas injection sites to maintain supply. Operations teams closely monitored system pressures and changing weather conditions, coordinating with neighboring utilities, emergency responders and local officials throughout the response.


The effort required extraordinary collaboration among gas operations, engineering, system control and numerous supporting teams, all working toward a common goal: protecting reliable natural gas service for customers.


On Nov. 19, crews successfully completed a temporary pipeline bypass across the river, restoring natural gas flow through the damaged corridor and marking a major milestone in the recovery effort.


The successful repair reflects weeks of determination, creative problem-solving and teamwork under exceptionally difficult circumstances.


While work remains to complete a permanent repair, the temporary bypass represents an important step toward restoring the system’s long-term resilience.
